clue.text: Quietly says "clubs"

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
utters means says

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs the word 'clubs', perhaps bidding at bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'clubs' look like the thing being said; it is the definition, golf clubs used on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers' short-game clubs used on the green are a kind of golf club.

clue.text: Charge after a mount for example

parts.note: post- is a prefix meaning after

indicators.note: to mount is to climb, so in a down clue the abbreviation is read from the bottom upward

explanation.surface: A fee added on after buying a horse, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like a horse; it is the up signal that turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fee paid for sending a letter is a charge.

clue.text: Radical change may be made in a trust for gain

indicators.note: something may be made from these letters by putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: Putting assets into a trust for profit transforms one's finances.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete metamorphosis is a fundamental alteration.

clue.text: Language — the queen's English

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A remark about the Queen's English.
explanation.walkthrough: ERSE is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaelic is a Celtic tongue.

clue.text: Heartless fool with aim to acquire a decoration

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letter of the word for fool is removed

parts.note: a sap is a fool
to angle for something is to aim at it

explanation.surface: A heartless idiot aims to win a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' drops the A from SAP, leaving SP, which takes in ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequin is a small glittering ornament sewn on clothes.

clue.text: Everybody not paid off will be given leave

parts.note: everybody means all
a debt not paid off is still owed

explanation.surface: A worker whose wages are still owed is granted time off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given leave is to be permitted, a synonym.

clue.text: Dexterity is needed getting a plug to line up

parts.note: an ad is a plug, a piece of advertising
to dress ranks is to line soldiers up

explanation.surface: Skill is required to get a plug lined up with a socket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' suggests an electrical plug; it is an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill or adroitness, as in handling something with address, is a sense of the word.

clue.text: The diver left with nothing on

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A diver departs without any clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: The diver is a bird: in North America the great northern diver is called a loon.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving waterbird is the North American name for the diver.

clue.text: Hardly inspiring!

parts.note: reads as faint criticism of something dull, but means barely breathing in, from suspense

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on something dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiting anxiously, a person scarcely draws air, so they are hardly breathing in.

clue.text: He's given a rod, not new

indicators.note: making the letters new means forming them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man receives a fishing rod that is second-hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's given' reads as he receives, but means he has given, one who gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has donated is a giver, a benefactor.

clue.text: Non-synthetic stuff isn't sold at once — a problem

indicators.note: a problem leaves things in disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A trader laments that their natural fabric won't sell straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges ISNTSOLDATONCE plus A (the apostrophe is no letter) into the fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine long-staple cotton grown on islands off the American south-east is a natural, not man-made, fabric.

clue.text: Some cereals ought to be included

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dietary instruction that some cereals should be part of the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something included as well is in addition, the same idea as 'too' or 'besides'.

clue.text: Silver grass all over the place

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a ley is land put down to grass for a time

explanation.surface: Silvery grass growing untidily everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: AGLEY is Scots for awry, best known from Burns's line about the best-laid schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word meaning askew or gone wrong, so in disarray.

clue.text: Come up against a barring

parts.note: but in 'all but one' means barring, except

explanation.surface: A rugby player is stopped by a tackle unless there is a bar in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To border on or touch something is to meet it at an edge.

clue.text: Small players fume

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Junior players lose their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapour rising from something hot is a fume.

clue.text: Nettle fabric

explanation.surface: A stinging plant woven into cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle is to irritate or offend; it is also a ribbed cotton fabric.

clue.text: A record one lets play when writing

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: letting the word lets play loosely means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A record company lets one track play while somebody writes.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter, especially a formal or biblical one, is a piece of writing.

clue.text: Quicker to see point in a riddle

indicators.note: in places the compass point inside the word for a riddle

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, something that sifts
W, west, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone sharper at catching the point of a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' suggests a puzzle, but here it is a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Faster and more rapid mean the same thing.

clue.text: Calamitous used-car war

indicators.note: a calamitous state is a disastrous mess, so these letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A disastrous battle over second-hand vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign waged with zeal, originally a holy war, is a kind of war.

clue.text: The French entering the civil service — so exemplary

indicators.note: entering says the French article goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: la is French for the
sic is Latin for so, thus

explanation.surface: Joining the civil service makes the French a model of good behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serving as a standard model is a typical, outstanding example.

clue.text: Passed a note with drinks to a top newsman

parts.note: E is a musical note
laps means drinks, as a cat does
the editor, ED, is the top person in a newsroom

explanation.surface: A note is passed along with drinks to a senior journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has gone by has elapsed, so slipped past.

clue.text: The accumulation of stock

parts.note: reads like a business stockpile, but refers to cattle gathered in by cowboys

explanation.surface: A dry business phrase about building up inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranchers herd livestock together in a gathering of cattle, so stock is collected.

clue.text: Do without, which can be a burden

explanation.surface: Doing without something can feel like carrying a load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' looks like a load; it is the old sense of a song's chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to do without; a repeated chorus is also called a burden.

clue.text: A sea-god would get upset or troubled

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A sea deity grows angry or disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The shape-shifting old man of the sea in Greek myth is a marine deity.

clue.text: A container not completely closed

parts.note: a jar is a container

explanation.surface: A lid left on a pot that does not quite seal.
explanation.definitionFit: A door slightly open is not fully shut.

clue.text: There's a prohibition on very loud music in Scotland

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Loud music is forbidden north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: BANFF is a town on the north-east coast of Scotland; the definition is the brief 'in Scotland', standing for a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: A small town in Aberdeenshire is a place in that country.

clue.text: The old ship has a right to proceed

parts.note: go means to proceed

explanation.surface: An old vessel is given permission to sail.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth, Jason and his Argonauts sailed in this vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason's legendary vessel is an ancient ship of myth.

clue.text: Estimate speed

explanation.surface: Judging how fast something goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate is to estimate value; rate also means a pace or velocity.

clue.text: Taking wrong turning, don't hang about!

indicators.note: turning says the word for a wrong is read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A driver who takes a wrong turn is told to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To move briskly, at a jogging pace, is to hurry rather than linger.

clue.text: Round and round it goes, up and down

definitions.text: Round and round it goes, up and down

parts.words: Round and round it goes, up and down
parts.note: sounds like a fairground ride, but describes steps winding about a central post between floors

explanation.surface: A description of a merry-go-round or roller coaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Steps coiling around a column between floors carry climbers in circles as they rise or descend.

clue.text: Following swindle show an inclination to fight

indicators.note: following says the second piece comes after the word for swindle

parts.note: a con is a swindle
to tend is to be inclined

explanation.surface: After being cheated, someone feels like starting a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle or compete against someone is to battle.

clue.text: Not lacking in inches, so scores

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: lacking says the little word in is removed from the word inches

explanation.surface: A boastful claim about height that doubles as a tally of points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes IN from INCHES, leaving CHES.
explanation.definitionFit: A score was once kept by cutting marks on a tally stick, so marks and scores are synonyms.
